issues.legal_issue: An unrestricted grant of property to a spouse, coupled with a power of alienation, conveys an absolute estate when the will’s other provisions concern only income.
material_facts: The will stated that the property would vest in the testator’s wife with power of alienation.
Other clauses provided for maintenance of a family place of worship and for investment and sharing of surplus income, but did not distribute the property itself.
The will made a specific provision for the other heirs to share income, while making no corresponding provision for them to share the property.
issues.conclusion: The wife received an absolute estate in the property.
issues.legal_principle: A will must be construed to ascertain the testator’s intention from its provisions as a whole. An express, unrestricted power of alienation supports an absolute grant, and provisions allocating income do not limit the estate in the corpus. Reconciliation of clauses may be necessary where provisions conflict, as recognized in Navneet Lal alias Rangi v. Gokul, but the Court found no inconsistency here.

predicates.will_grants_property_to_spouse_with_powe: The testator’s will gives property to a spouse and expressly allows the spouse to alienate it.
predicates.other_clauses_allocate_income_only: The other relevant provisions deal with income from the property rather than ownership of the property itself.
predicates.recipient_takes_absolute_estate: The recipient takes the property as an absolute owner.

issues.definition: When a will grants property to a spouse with power of alienation and its other relevant clauses allocate income only, the recipient takes an absolute estate.

issues.legal_issue: An absolute estate carries the right to dispose of the property by a later will without a separate grant of testamentary power.
material_facts: The wife received an absolute estate under her husband’s will.
She later made a will disposing of the property she had received.
The validity of that disposition was contested in a property claim.
issues.conclusion: The wife was entitled to dispose of the property by her own will.
issues.legal_principle: The unrestricted power to dispose of property is an incident of an absolute estate and includes testamentary disposition; separate authorization to make a will is unnecessary. A restraint on alienation attached to an absolute grant is void.

predicates.later_will_disposition_is_contested_in_p: A claim concerning property challenges a recipient’s later disposition of that property by will.
predicates.recipient_has_absolute_estate: The recipient holds the property as an absolute owner.
predicates.recipient_can_dispose_of_property_by_wil: The recipient is entitled to dispose of the property by will.

issues.definition: When a property claim contests a later testamentary disposition and the recipient holds an absolute estate, the recipient can dispose of the property by will.

issues.legal_issue: A bequest to a wife alone is not taken as tavazhi property when the will shows a contrary intention by giving her the property as her own with power of alienation.
material_facts: The testator bequeathed the property to his wife alone.
The will stated that she would take it as her own property with power of alienation.
The will separately provided for other heirs to share surplus income, but did not provide for them to share the property itself.
issues.conclusion: The property was the wife’s individual property and was not taken as tavazhi property.
issues.legal_principle: Section 48 of the Madras Marumakkattayam Act, 1932 provides that a bequest to a wife alone is taken as tavazhi property by the wife and her children unless a contrary intention appears from the will. The will’s express provision that the property was the wife’s own, coupled with the power of alienation and the separate treatment of income, showed a contrary intention.

predicates.bequest_is_to_wife_alone: The testator bequeaths the property to his wife alone.
predicates.will_shows_property_is_her_own_with_alie: The will indicates that the wife takes the property as her own and may alienate it.
predicates.property_is_individual_not_tavazhi_prope: The property belongs to the wife individually rather than as tavazhi property.

issues.definition: When a bequest is to a wife alone but the will shows that the property is her own and may be alienated, the property is individual rather than tavazhi property.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory provision preserving customary law does not determine a dispute that turns on the construction of a will where no conflict between the statute and custom arises.
material_facts: The parties were governed by the Madras Marumakkattayam Act, 1932.
The dispute turned on whether the testator’s will gave his wife an absolute estate.
No competition between the Act and any rule of law, custom, or usage was involved.
issues.conclusion: Section 50 of the Act did not affect the issue the Court had to decide.
issues.legal_principle: Section 50 provides that the Act does not affect rules of Marumakkattayam law, custom, or usage except to the extent expressly stated in the Act. The Court held that this saving provision did not bear on the construction of the will where no conflict with such a rule, custom, or usage was presented.

predicates.dispute_turns_on_will_construction: The dispute depends on what estate the testator’s will created.
predicates.no_conflict_with_customary_rule_is_invol: No conflict between the governing statute and a rule of custom or usage is presented.
predicates.customary_law_saving_clause_does_not_det: The provision preserving customary rules does not determine the construction of the will.

issues.definition: When a dispute turns on construing a will and involves no conflict with a customary rule, the customary-law saving clause does not determine that construction.
